findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow uses String for status plus separate bool flags (is_validated, is_sent), allowing illegal combinations such as is_validated=false, is_sent=true, status="draft". The type does not enforce the lifecycle invariant that a budget must be validated before it can be sent.
findings.failure_mode: Any consumer reading BudgetWorkflow cannot trust its state; invariants must be re-checked at every use site, leading to missed checks and undefined system behavior
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single enum typestate (e.g., enum BudgetState { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at: Timestamp } }). Make all fields private. Provide fallible constructors or constructors that guarantee valid states.

findings.problem: id is a raw String. Domain IDs carry rules (uniqueness, format, lifetime) that a String cannot enforce. This is primitive obsession.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid, duplicate, or format-violating IDs are silently accepted; no domain-level guard exists
findings.fix: Introduce a BudgetId newtype with a private inner field and a fallible constructor that validates the ID format at the parse boundary.

findings.problem: status is a raw String instead of an enum. String status allows typos, unknown values, and values outside the defined lifecycle (e.g., status="sent" while is_sent=false).
findings.failure_mode: Unknown or mismatched status values cause silent logic errors; string comparison is fragile and not exhaustive
findings.fix: Replace with an exhaustive enum (Draft, Validated, Sent). Use match for exhaustive handling.

findings.problem: is_validated is a standalone bool that does not form a type-enforced lifecycle step. It is redundant with status when status is an enum, or meaningless when status is a string.
findings.failure_mode: The boolean can be true while status is not in a validated state, creating contradictory state that downstream logic cannot safely reason about
findings.fix: Merge into the BudgetState typestate enum (e.g., BudgetState::Validated). Remove the standalone bool field entirely.

findings.problem: is_sent is a standalone bool that duplicates information already implied by status="sent". It is redundant and can diverge from status.
findings.failure_mode: is_sent=true with status="draft" represents a contradictory state; consumers must check both fields and can miss one
findings.fix: Merge into the BudgetState typestate enum (e.g., BudgetState::Sent { sent_at: Timestamp }). Remove the standalone bool field entirely.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> without a dedicated timestamp newtype. It has no bounds, no timezone semantics, and no validation of the epoch format.
findings.failure_mode: Zero, negative (if i64), or impossibly large epoch values are silently accepted; no domain meaning is encoded
findings.fix: Replace with a TimestampOrEpochMs newtype with a fallible constructor, or use chrono/TimeSystem if the crate already depends on a time crate.

findings.problem: All fields of BudgetWorkflow are pub. Any code in the crate can construct arbitrary invalid states by directly assigning fields, completely bypassing invariants.
findings.failure_mode: The type provides zero encapsulation; callers can set is_sent=true while leaving status="draft", creating invalid states that the type claims to represent
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide constructors (e.g., BudgetWorkflow::draft()) and state-transition methods (e.g., .validate(), .send()) that enforce the typestate machine.

findings.problem: mark_sent is a free function that takes ownership and mutates fields directly. It is infallible, does not check preconditions (e.g., is the budget validated?), and bypasses the typestate machine entirely.
findings.failure_mode: A budget can be sent without ever being validated, or multiple times, with no guard. The function cannot express failure modes like BudgetError::NotValidated or BudgetError::AlreadySent
findings.fix: Convert mark_sent into a method on BudgetWorkflow that takes self into BudgetState::Validated and returns Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError>. Gate on the typestate to prevent sending non-validated budgets.

findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow mixes data with a mutating free function. There is no functional core boundary — the struct is a mutable data bag and mark_sent is imperative shell code operating on it directly. No pure domain logic exists.
findings.failure_mode: Logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation from I/O or side effects; the type offers no deterministic core
findings.fix: Define a pure BudgetData type (serializable, no I/O). Implement state transitions as pure functions BudgetData -> Result<BudgetData, BudgetError>. Shell code handles persistence, RPC, and event emission around the pure core.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no return error type. The error taxonomy from the domain (NotValidated, AlreadySent, Overflow) does not exist. No FallibleResult type alias or typed error enum is defined.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot pattern-match on specific failure modes; errors are silently lost or converted to panics downstream
findings.fix: Define an enum BudgetError { NotValidated, AlreadySent, Allocation } with a FallibleResult<T> = Result<T, BudgetError> alias. Use ? with map_err at boundaries.

findings.problem: No benchmark module exists. There is no baseline measurement for any performance claim on BudgetWorkflow or mark_sent.
findings.failure_mode: Any future optimization or refactor has no measured baseline; performance regressions go undetected
findings.fix: Add a benches/ module with criterion or similar, measuring mark_sent latency and throughput under realistic payload sizes.

findings.problem: No profiler evidence exists. Hot paths in BudgetWorkflow are not profiled with flamegraphs or similar.
findings.failure_mode: Hot-path allocations and CPU bottlenecks are invisible
findings.fix: Add flamegraph or perf profiling for the hot path; report allocation count and CPU time.

findings.problem: No allocation tracking exists. mark_sent creates a String via "sent".to_string() on every call, allocating heap memory for a known string literal. No try_reserve or capacity planning is used anywhere.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every mark_sent call; no evidence that this allocation budget is acceptable
findings.fix: Use &'static str for status instead of allocating a String. If a mutable string is required, pass &mut str or use a pre-allocated buffer.

findings.problem: No second-ring evidence (assembly output, SBOM, baseline revision) exists to verify zero-cost or performance claims.
findings.failure_mode: Any performance claim cannot be independently verified
findings.fix: Add cargo expand --release assembly output for mark_sent, and document baseline revision and target hardware.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or BudgetWorkflow
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis
no allocation tracking or instrumented allocation count
no second-ring evidence (assembly, SBOM, baseline revision) for performance or zero-cost claims
no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test were not run
residual_risk: The crate has systemic architectural violations: no typestate, no typed errors, no encapsulation, no functional core boundary, and all fields are public with primitive types. This allows any illegal state combination (e.g., not-validated but sent). Static review only — no commands were run. The crate will fail strict Holzman clippy and fmt gates once repaired. All findings are BLOCKER-level because they violate the core Holzman doctrine of making illegal states unrepresentable.
